novelty_claim: Adaptive refusal-triggered re-seeding plus population-coupled refinement: PAIR's streams refine their own dead branches in isolation for all K iterations. PAIR 2.0 (a) detects a hard-refusal turn (judge score 1 with refusal-marker response) and abandons that stream's branch, re-initializing it with the next unused attacker framing instead of refining a corpse; (b) couples the two streams by injecting the sibling stream's best-scoring (prompt, response, score) exemplar into the attacker's feedback each iteration, turning independent streams into a 2-island memetic search; (c) falls back to the secondary auxiliary model when the primary attacker's JSON never parses, recovering wasted turns.
initial_hypothesis: Refusal-triggered branch re-seeding + cross-stream best-exemplar sharing converts a meaningful share of the refusal-plateau class: mean ASR rises from the locked baseline 0.185 by >=50% relative (>=0.28) with <=6 target calls per goal (identical budget: 2 streams x 3 iterations), without reducing the 0.480 ASR the parent already achieves on gpt-5.6-luna.
key_insight: Consensus mining over 300 baseline trajectories (100 goals x 3 victims, s2i3): among scored failures, 106/110 never exceed judge score 1 across all 6 turns — the victim hard-refuses from iteration 1 and both streams keep refining the same rejected wrapper, since PAIR's feedback carries no gradient and streams never share information; strategy identity (roleplay vs logical) is irrelevant to escape rate. Excluding unscorable provider_error cases, the mechanism target is the refusal-plateau class, ~96% of failures on qwen3.7-flash, gpt-oss-120b, deepseek-v4-flash.
